import html from typing import List # Example template. In a real application this would be defined elsewhere. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{headline}

Posted by: {poster_name}

{text}
{tags}
""" def compose_post_html( poster_name: str, headline: str, text: str, hashtags: List[str] ) -> str: """ Construct a safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- poster_name : str The name of the author. headline : str The title/headline of the post. text : str The main body of the post. hashtags : list[str] A list of tags to be displayed. Returns ------- str An XSS‑protected HTML string containing the post. """ # Basic type checks – raise if inputs are not as expected if not isinstance(poster_name, str): raise TypeError("poster_name must be a string") if not isinstance(headline, str): raise TypeError("headline must be a string") if not isinstance(text, str): raise TypeError("text must be a string") if not (isinstance(hashtags, list) and all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in hashtags)): raise TypeError("hashtags must be a list of strings") # Escape user‑provided content to prevent XSS safe_poster_name = html.escape(poster_name, quote=True) safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_text = html.escape(text, quote=False) # Allow < > for formatting # Build the tags string – each tag wrapped in a safe_tags = ''.join(f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in hashtags) # Format the final HTML html_output = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster_name=safe_poster_name, headline=safe_headline, text=safe_text, tags=safe_tags ) return html_output.strip()
